headline: US stocks rose on Monday and the Nasdaq closed at a record, led by AI-related shares such as Nvidia and Microsoft, even though US government bond yields are at their highest since 2002.
score_reason: Pool score 7 kept: Monday's close is confirmed by Reuters and other outlets, and it pairs a record Nasdaq with the highest long-term yields since 2002.
importance_line: People with mortgages, pensions or share funds feel both the record share prices and the highest long-term borrowing costs since 2002, and the doubt is that the rally leans on AI profits that investors expect but companies have yet to report.
summary: Reuters reports that the tech-heavy Nasdaq index closed at a record on Monday, up 1.05% at 27,477.31, lifted by Nvidia and Microsoft, while the S&P 500 (a broad index of large US companies) rose 0.66% to 7,773.95, about 0.3% below its August record. TradingView News adds that the yield (interest rate) on 10-year US government bonds closed at 5.31%, the highest since 2002; this continues the Bloomberg story in our 5 Oct 2026 edition about AI stocks holding up against rising yields, and what is new today is the Nasdaq's first record close since 22 September.
notes: WSJ original (HTTP 401) not opened. Reuters text read on its AOL copy (https://www.aol.com/articles/wall-st-futures-dip-tech-104659000.html); the Reuters link is the live-updated market report found through Google News (its slug still carries the early-day headline) and was not opened. Yield figures from TradingView News; Chosunbiz gives the same index levels and an intraday 10-year high of 5.347%. Follow-up of our 5 Oct 2026 edition item on Bloomberg's 4 Oct report.
